recommendations.name: Stranger Things season 5
recommendations.blurb: Stranger Things occupies such a strange place in my brain. It has never been my favorite thing on TV, but I have devoured every season of it, and I can’t wait for the new season to start. Be prepared, though: it’s eight episodes, but it’s… a lot more than eight hours.

recommendations.name: Alton Brown Cooks Food .
recommendations.blurb: One of the all-time great TV cooking hosts is back, and doing it big on YouTube. The first episode , about cooking turkey, feels somehow both like a TV show and like a perfect YouTube video. He’s still got it.

recommendations.name: The Beatles Anthology 2025
recommendations.blurb: The original version of this series, from 30 years ago — which includes music, a documentary, and a book — was one of the things that made me love The Beatles in the first place. This version has been remastered, includes even more stuff, and is required consumption for any music fan anywhere.

recommendations.name: Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery
recommendations.blurb: Rian Johnson , Daniel Craig, and the rest of the Knives Out gang just don’t seem to miss. This one’s headed to theaters for a couple of weeks before hitting Netflix December 12th, and if I can I plan to see it in both places. I love a good whodunit, and these keep being good whodunits.

recommendations.name: Galactic
recommendations.blurb: I’ve seen this new comic series compared to Star Wars, True Romance, Tarantino movies, and a dozen other things. It’s violent, it’s sci-fi, it’s romance, it sounds pretty awesome.

recommendations.name: Amazon Leo Ultra
recommendations.blurb: Amazon’s Starlink competitor is finally shaping up to be a real thing, and a good thing at that: this new antenna doesn’t have a price yet but does promise up to 1Gbps of download speeds. If you’re shopping for satellite internet anytime soon, this could be a winner.

recommendations.name: Do You Feel Guilty about Bad Reviews?
recommendations.blurb: “ Do You Feel Guilty about Bad Reviews? ” Two top-notch creators, Michael Fisher and Marques Brownlee, talking about AI and politics and the creator economy and life after platforms. So much to learn in this for anyone interested in tech, or life as a creator.

recommendations.name: Xbox Crocs
recommendations.blurb: Listen, I like a silly brand integration as much as the next guy, but this? This is next level. It’s Crocs! With buttons! And joysticks! If I can get my hands on a pair these will become my official Gaming Footwear.

recommendations.name: Claude Opus 4.5.
recommendations.blurb: Claude is consistently one of the best all-around LLMs, but generally what I hear is that it is at its best when it’s coding. And Opus 4.5 appears to be a big step up in what Claude Code can do. Time to finally finish vibe-coding my perfect productivity app, maybe?

recommendations.name: The Nintendo Switch 2
recommendations.blurb: Hands down the best gadget I bought this year. If this thing only played Mario Kart World, Donkey Kong Bananza, and Kirby Air Riders, I’d probably still be happy with it. But the library is huge! And getting huger! I’m gaming every day in a way I haven’t in a long time.

recommendations.name: The POP Phone
recommendations.blurb: Hands down the silliest gadget I bought this year, that nevertheless brings me tremendous joy. It plugs into a USB-C port (presumably on your phone) and gives you that old-school landline feel. Way more comfortable than pressing my phone to my ear, and sounds good too.

recommendations.name: Baseus USB cables
recommendations.blurb: I’m still carrying around two of these retractable beasts as my only two charging cables, and it’s still working great. Though I confess, I am tempted by the model that also has the charging brick built in .

recommendations.name: The Hoto Electric Screwdriver
recommendations.blurb: I swear, this is the Black Friday deal of the year every year, and I completely get why. It’s powerful enough for most simple tasks, charges via USB-C, lasts forever — it’s my most-used tool by a mile. (You can spend more to get one with a screen, but… why.)

recommendations.name: The Doorman
recommendations.blurb: The most un-put-down-able book I read this year. It unfolds in the most unusual way, and almost seems like it can’t possibly all come together in a satisfying way. But oh, boy, does it ever.

recommendations.name: The Logitech UE Wonderboom
recommendations.blurb: There are a million Bluetooth speakers out there, but nothing beats this squat little dude when it comes to battery life, durability, waterproofing, and sound quality. I have one in the bathroom, one in my travel bag, and one… somewhere else. I lost it. It’ll turn up.

recommendations.name: Acquire
recommendations.blurb: I rediscovered this decades-old board game this year, and was reminded of how much I love it! It’s a simple premise — you’re building and merging hotel chains, one building at a time — but it requires exactly the right amount of thinking and strategy.

recommendations.name: Wits & Wagers
recommendations.blurb: My family randomly encountered this game at a winery one weekend, and it was a huge hit. It’s sort of a trivia game, sort of a betting game, sort of Apples to Apples -ish. I can’t remember a game that went over this well with my entire family.

recommendations.name: Google’s Pixel Buds 2a
recommendations.blurb: I don’t know what it is about these headphones. I have so many other headphones! But I keep picking these. They’re small and light, sound good, feel good in my ears, and if I’m honest, I really do love the purple.

recommendations.name: The Away Overnight Bag.
recommendations.blurb: If I’m traveling for between 12 hours and four days, this is the bag I take. It has a few pockets and a laptop sleeve, and a surprisingly roomy spot for all my clothes.

recommendations.name: Philips Hue Essential bulbs
recommendations.blurb: I bought a bunch of these just recently, at my colleague Jen Tuohy’s recommendation, and they’re exactly what I need: relatively affordable, easy to set up, compatible with everything. I don’t want to think at all about my lightbulbs, you know? I don’t think about these anymore.

recommendations.name: The Brick
recommendations.blurb: For some reason, this thing just works for me: I have a Brick in my office and another in the kitchen, and just by tapping my phone on the little cube I’m able to turn my phone to a more minimalist mode. I should use it more, but I use it a lot.

recommendations.name: The M4 Mac Mini
recommendations.blurb: This is obviously a bigger purchase, but it is also the computer I recommend to almost everyone looking to upgrade their desktop. This combination of price and power is absolutely ridiculous — I have one as my daily driver and I couldn’t be happier.

recommendations.name: iPhone 17 Pro
recommendations.blurb: The phone: iPhone 17 Pro.

recommendations.name: Spark
recommendations.blurb: I’ve been playing the daily games from Spark . They’ve been great and I’ve been learning things along the way. I love the daily learning habit it’s creating for me.

recommendations.name: Dungeon Crawler Carl
recommendations.blurb: All about world immersion for me this week. Been reading the first Dungeon Crawler Carl . Super fun and like reading a video game. Accidentally fell down a Kingdom Come Deliverance rabbit hole. Got the new one on sale and decided it was so good that I had to get the first one and play that instead.

recommendations.name: 4K Criterion release of Eyes Wide Shut
recommendations.blurb: Come on, it’s the 4K Criterion release of Eyes Wide Shut , obviously!

recommendations.name: Viwoods AIPaper Reader
recommendations.blurb: Really considering getting a Viwoods AIPaper Reader . Like a Boox Palma, but Carta 1300, Android 16, etc. Waiting on battery tests though.

recommendations.name: The Division 2
recommendations.blurb: The Division 2 , the video game. Yes, it’s about seven years old now, but it’s still got a huge user base and the dev team is rolling out new stuff all the time. In like a month’s time the game is getting a total redesign to add some things the users have been asking for.

recommendations.name: The Great Work
recommendations.blurb: The Great Work , the debut novel from Sheldon Costa, was my most recent fantastic read.

recommendations.name: Home Assistant
recommendations.blurb: Home Assistant because, apparently, home automation is my new hobby and I like the idea of local control. Shouldn’t be too long before I’ve locked myself inside my house.

recommendations.name: Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End
recommendations.blurb: Catching up with Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End before Season 2 hits. It’s an anime that starts where most end: the 10-year quest is over and we see where the party members go from there. It might be the show with the most heart airing right now, and it’s beautiful to look at.

recommendations.name: In Stars And Time
recommendations.blurb: I just started In Stars And Time , a black and white RPG with the best character writing I’ve seen in years. Even the annoying character is adorable by the end of the first hour.

recommendations.name: in 24 minutes
recommendations.blurb: I mentioned above that Stranger Things is back this week. I’m excited! It’s also been roughly 648 years since the last season debuted. Luckily, YouTube exists, so rather than try to plow through every episode again I’ve been watching a bunch of series recaps.
